pl-l2d19c2-d1e108.summary: Explains that in the first state the body was animal, needing food; man was made 'a living soul,' giving life to a body that was animal, not spiritual, sustained by food; so the body was mortal and immortal, able to die and not to die.
claims: The first body was animal and needed food.

pl-l2d19c2-d1e113.summary: States that after sin the body became 'dead' (Rom 8:10), having the necessity of dying; in the resurrection it will be spiritual, agile, needing no food, and immortal so that it cannot die.
claims: After sin the body must die.

pl-l2d19c2-d1e116.summary: Cites Augustine: the body was first animal, formed from earth; we will rise not to that but to a spiritual body, into which Adam would have been changed had he not merited death by sinning. Paul says not 'mortal because of sin' but 'dead.'
claims: Adam would have passed to a spiritual body without dying.

pl-l2d19c2.summary: Explains that in the first state the body was animal, needing food; man was made a 'living soul' (Gen 2:7), giving life to the body through food, and so mortal and immortal. After sin it became 'dead,' having the necessity of dying (Rom 8:10). In the resurrection it will be spiritual, agile, not needing food, and immortal in that it cannot die. Augustine: Adam would have been changed into a spiritual body without death had he not sinned; Paul says the body is 'dead,' not 'mortal,' because of sin.
claims: Before sin the body was animal, needing food.
After sin the body is 'dead,' having the necessity of dying.
The risen body will be spiritual, agile, needing no food, and unable to die.
Had Adam not sinned he would have been changed into a spiritual body without death.
